question.text: Rajesh (age 40) wants to retire at 60 with monthly expenses of Rs. 60,000 (in today's terms). Inflation is 7% p.a. and expected investment return during retirement is 9% p.a. He plans for 25 years in retirement. Using the inflation-adjusted return method, what retirement corpus does Rajesh need at age 60?

explanation.text: The Logic: Step 1: Monthly expense at retirement = Rs. 60,000 x (1.07)^20 = approximately Rs. 2,32,181, giving an annual expense of approximately Rs. 27,86,173. Step 2: Real (inflation-adjusted) return = ((1.09)/(1.07)) - 1 = 1.8692% p.a. Step 3: PV of annuity for 25 years at 1.8692% = (1 - (1.018692)^(-25)) / 0.018692 = approximately 19.8267. Step 4: Corpus = Rs. 27,86,173 x 19.8267 = approximately Rs. 5,52,40,592, or about Rs. 5.52 crore. The Trap: Rs. 3.85 crore results from not inflating the monthly expense to the retirement date — applying Rs. 60,000 x 12 x 19.83 directly. Rs. 6.30 crore uses the nominal return of 9% instead of the inflation-adjusted real return. Note: The inflation-adjusted return method (using the real return as the discount rate on the inflation-adjusted first-year withdrawal) is the standard retirement-corpus calculation the workbook teaches.
